paragraphs: Sumkhos, Mishnah, beginning of BaKol Me'arvin; Bava Metzia 6:5; Oto VeEt Beno, in R. Meir's name, Mishnah, 82a [source locator]. He was R. Meir's principal student. After R. Meir died, R. Yehudah ordered his students excluded from the study house as contentious; Sumkhos pressed in, Kiddushin 52b; Nazir 49b. Eruvin 13b: he gave forty-eight reasons for every matter of impurity and purity, very incisive like his teacher. He was Rabbi's colleague—Yuḥasin's transmission list from Yesod Olam with Rema's glosses—and from the Land (see Natan the Babylonian). A baraita: Sumkhos ben Yose. Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Berakhot 2, and Alfasi there: Sumkhos bar Yosef, 'Whoever prolongs eḥad has his days prolonged.' Babylonian Berakhot 13b attributes it to Sumkhos without patronymic; Heilprin considers Asheri’s bar Issi a scribal error. R. Abba said he asked Sumkhos, Ketubbot 81a; this R. Abba is Abba Arikha (see his entry). Yehudah ben Nakosa. R. Natan asked him.
